scope_notes.value: Institutions, stations, laboratories, programmes and networks through which scientific work in Panama was organized and sustained.
Observation, description, collection and classification of plants, animals, fungi and other natural phenomena in historical scientific practice.
Knowledge of biological diversity in Panama, including taxonomy, distribution, systematics, specimen evidence and changing classifications.
Research on ecological relationships, populations, communities, habitats, ecosystem processes and organism-environment interactions.
Historical relationships among environments, human action, scientific knowledge, infrastructure and changing landscapes in Panama.
Production and use of spatial knowledge about Panama, including mapping, surveying, boundaries, localities and georeferencing.
Medical, epidemiological and public-health knowledge and intervention in Panama, including disease surveillance, sanitation and health institutions.

scope_notes.value: Production, repetition, criticism and transformation of historical and scientific narratives about Panama.
Scientific work conducted through direct observation, collection, measurement or intervention outside the principal laboratory or office.
Systematic acquisition of specimens, samples or other natural-history material for research and collections.
A research practice and institutional form organized around sustained scientific work at a field site. Named stations remain entities.
Material and technical systems that enable sustained research, observation, experimentation, storage or communication.
Labor required to produce scientific knowledge, including field, laboratory, technical, clerical, maintenance and support work.
Correspondence used to produce, coordinate, circulate or interpret scientific knowledge.
Movement of specimens among collectors, institutions, collections and researchers.
Processes through which specimens are identified, determined, redetermined or reconciled with taxonomic knowledge.
Historical transition among predecessor, successor, renamed or reorganized institutions.
Formation, movement, division, use and reinterpretation of documentary, material, biological or living collections.
Arrangement, interfiling, reclassification or reconstruction of archival records and the research consequences of those interventions.
Programmes and practices intended to reduce malaria transmission, morbidity or mortality.
Interventions directed at organisms that transmit disease, including environmental and chemical methods.
Administrative, infrastructural and environmental practices intended to improve public health conditions.
Modification or maintenance of water flow and standing water for health, infrastructure or environmental purposes.
Use of larvicidal substances to control mosquito or other vector larvae.
Distribution or administration of quinine as prophylactic or therapeutic public-health practice.
Systematic observation, recording and analysis of disease occurrence for public-health action.
Production and use of quantitative measures concerning morbidity, mortality, admissions, populations and related health conditions.
Administrative or statistical categorization of populations for measurement, governance or institutional reporting.
Deliberate or consequential alteration of landscapes, hydrology, vegetation or habitats through human intervention.
Movement and establishment of plant material outside a previous cultivation or geographic context, without assuming later naturalization.
Plant genetic resources maintained, exchanged or studied as accessions, lines, cultivars or related biological material.
Documented movement of living biological material among institutions, sites, collections or programmes.
Production of new living plant material by seed, cutting, grafting or other reproductive techniques.
Cultivation undertaken to test performance, adaptation, breeding, yield or other research questions.
Exchange or circulation of seed material among institutions, programmes or individuals.
Historical practice or interpretation concerning the adaptation of introduced organisms to new environmental conditions.
Establishment of introduced organisms in self-sustaining populations outside cultivation or deliberate maintenance.
Expansion of introduced organisms with ecological, economic or management significance.
Repetition, quotation, paraphrase, translation or transformation through which a historical or scientific claim travels across sources.
Research process through which the identity of a historical person, place, object, institution or source is reconstructed.
Production and recording of quantitative observations through defined instruments, units or procedures.
Repeated observation or measurement intended to track conditions or change through time.
Practices through which entities, observations, people or evidence are organized into categories.
Naming, describing and classifying biological taxa and revising their relationships.
Routine technical and material work required to keep scientific, medical or infrastructural systems functioning.
Situated technical or experiential competence recognized or used in knowledge production and practice.
